stories.headline: Cyclone Murasu: Andhra Pradesh CM orders swift power restoration, price control measures
stories.title: Cyclone Murasu: Andhra Pradesh CM orders swift power restoration, price control measures
stories.summary: Naidu tells officials to monitor field-level relief operations, complete damage assessments at the earliest and esnure prompt financial assistance to the affected families
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has directed the officials to expedite relief and restoration operations in the areas affected by Cyclone Murasu, ensure prompt financial assistance to the victims and take steps to prevent a rise in the prices of essential commodities.

During a review meeting at his camp office on Saturday, Mr. Naidu assessed the damage caused by Cyclone Murasu and enquired about the progress of power restoration works, distribution of essential supplies and assessment of crop losses.
He instructed officials to closely monitor field-level relief operations and complete damage assessments at the earliest.
The officials informed Mr. Naidu that nearly 92% of the assessment of horticultural crop damage had been completed, while the same for agricultural crops would be completed by November 9.
Detailing the power restoration work, the officials said around 30,000 electricity poles damaged during Cyclone Arnav had been repaired, and power supply had been restored to all affected villages.
Following Cyclone Murasu, the restoration work is underway in 1,825 villages, with 7,850 damaged poles already repaired, they said.
The Civil Supplies Department officials said that essential commodities had been distributed to 3.82 lakh affected families so far.
Mr. Naidu also reviewed the measures to regulate prices of onions, rice, palm oil, red gram dal and wheat flour.
Officials said onions were being sold at ₹35 per kg through Rythu Bazaars, with 8,000 quintals of produce procured for the purpose.
Traders had agreed to sell different rice varieties at government-fixed prices ranging from ₹47 to ₹82 per kg.
Cases had been registered against 204 traders for violating government directives, they said.
Officials further informed Mr. Naidu that subsidised rice was being sold through 150 counters at Rythu Bazaars.

stories.headline: Nepal releases details of 2,294 nationals, 171 foreigners missing after August 26 floods
stories.title: Nepal releases details of 2,294 nationals, 171 foreigners missing after August 26 floods
stories.summary: Kathmandu, Nov 7: Nepal on Saturday released details of 2,294 nationals from 32 districts, along with 171 foreign nationals from seven countries, who went missing after a devastating flood hit the Himalayan nation on August 26. The move comes a month after the government ended the 40-day search and rescue operation for victims of the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli floods, which killed at least 1,455 people and left 5,285 missing, according to Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA). The authority said the list includes only those whose missing status has been verified by the respective District Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Committees. No further details were available about the remaining missing people who were not named in Saturday's list. The disaster management authority requested that if any individual listed as missing is found to be alive or has been located, they -- or their immediate family members -- should submit a claim within seven days. The highest number of missing Nepali nationals, 1,538, are from Rasuwa district, according to the list released by the NDRRMA. The NDRRMA has also released details of 171 missing foreign nationals from seven countries, excluding India. The authority's website has the complete list. Among them, 54 are from Malaysia and Ukraine, 33 from Australia, 11 from Russia, nine from South Korea, eight from Germany and two from Italy. The NDRRMA said it had not yet received a confirmed list of missing Indian nationals from the Indian Embassy. The list of missing Nepali nationals was prepared based on recommendations from the local governments where they had permanent residence and subsequently approved by the respective District Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Committees. For missing foreign nationals, the information was obtained through the Department of Consular Services and diplomatic missions based in Nepal or those designated to oversee the country, the authority said. The NDRRMA will issue a revised notice after receiving details from district administration offices across the 32 districts and relevant diplomatic missions on missing foreign nationals. Nepal ended the 40-day search-and-rescue operation for victims of the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli floods on October 5, shifting its focus to rehabilitation and reconstruction in the affected areas. The flash floods originated near the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26 and devastated towns and villages in northern and central Nepal. The Bhotekoshi River, which flows south from the Himalayan border region, carried the floodwaters downstream, sweeping away homes, vehicles, roads and bridges and damaging hydropower projects.

stories.title: Andhra Pradesh MPTC, ZPTC election results highlights: NDA continues its winning streak
stories.summary: The victory of NDA candidates across Andhra Pradesh is a testament to the aspirations of the people, says Roads and Buildings Minister B. C. Janardhan Reddy

article_sentences: - November 07, 2026 21:23NDA grabs 117 MPTC seats in Bapatla district, TDP wins 109The ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA), comprising Telugu Desam Party (TDP), Jana Sena Party (JSP) and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), registered a decisive victory in the MPTC elections in Bapatla district by winning 117 seats of the 273 MPTCs taken up for counting of votes.
According to the updates received till the last report came in on Saturday, the TDP secured 109 MPTC seats, while its alliance partner JSP won eight.
The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) secured 19 seats, while others won one.
The BJP did not register a victory in the results declared so far.

The result assumed significance as Bondapalli falls under the Gajapathinagaram Assembly constituency, represented by Minister for MSME Kondapalli Srinivas.
Ms. Anusha is also in charge of the Bheemili Assembly constituency in Visakhapatnam district.

Sharmila has congratulated former MLA and senior Congress leader Amanchi Krishna Mohan on the party’s performance in the Chirala Municipality elections, in which it won 10 of the 44 councillor seats.

In a statement, Ms. Sharmila praised Mr. Krishna Mohan, who is also the Bapatla District Congress Committee president and a member of the State Political Affairs Committee (PAC), for his efforts to strengthen the party in Chirala.
The Congress contested 42 wards and secured second place in several others.

Describing the party’s performance as a moral victory, Ms. Sharmila said the results demonstrated the Congress’s potential to emerge as a political alternative, despite failing to capture control of the municipality.

She thanked voters, party workers and elected councillors for their support and urged the newly elected councillors to function as an effective Opposition by consistently raising public issues and holding the ruling alliance accountable.

stories.title: Madras HC refuses to reject Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi’s election petition
stories.summary: Justice K. Kumaresh Babu dismisses an application filed by Thiruverumbur TVK MLA Vijayakumar alias Navalpattu Viji to reject the election petition
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Madras High Court has refused to reject an election petition filed by former Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi of the DMK challenging the victory of TVK MLA Vijayakumar alias Navalapattu Viji from Thiruverumbur Assembly constituency in the 2026 election.

Justice K. Kumaresh Babu said the Election Commission of India’s instructions to not engage children in election campaigns had a statutory force and, hence, the veracity of the allegation levelled against the MLA of having engaged children for his campaign could be tested only during trial.
The judge dismissed an application filed by the MLA to reject the petition.
Mr. Vijayakumar had won the seat by a margin of 8,705 votes.
He had secured 89,837 votes as against 81,132 votes garnered by the election petitioner who was his nearest rival candidate.

stories.headline: Uri’s Jalil Lone selected for UN climate summit
stories.title: Uri’s Jalil Lone selected for UN climate summit
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 07: Coming from a small and far-flung town of Uri, Jalil Lone, a humanitarian professional from Bijhama area in north Kashmir has been selected as a registered observer at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), scheduled to be held in Antalya, Türkiye, from November 9 to 20, 2026. With nearly two decades of experience working with communities affected by disasters and climate change, Jalil’s participation in the global climate summit is expected to provide another opportunity to highlight the concerns and experiences of vulnerable communities in international climate discussions. Currently based in Berlin, Germany, Jalil serves as Global Advisor on Disaster Risk Reduction, Climate Change and Anticipatory Action with DKH. In this capacity, he provides technical guidance and support to local partners, governments and civil society organisations across several disaster-prone regions. His professional responsibilities have taken him across Africa, the Middle East, Asia and Latin America, including Madagascar, Mozambique, Chad, Niger, Cameroon, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Syria, Yemen, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, Indonesia, the Philippines, Colombia and Haiti. Beyond his field-level humanitarian engagements, Jalil has also represented and led government delegations at several international conferences and dialogue platforms focusing on disaster risk reduction and climate resilience. His international engagements have included forums in Australia, Austria, the Philippines, Berlin and Geneva, where discussions centred on strengthening disaster preparedness and protecting communities vulnerable to climate-related risks. Recently, he visited Indonesia to engage with local partners on drought and dry-spell challenges. He subsequently travelled to Türkiye, where he participated in training programmes in Istanbul for civil society organisations and government representatives, including participants from Afghanistan and Pakistan. Reflecting on his demanding international schedule, Jalil said his work gave him immense satisfaction. “I am happy about the new responsibility. The travel is fun, but sometimes I run out of suitcases,” he remarked with a touch of humour. Throughout his career, Jalil has worked with several internationally recognised humanitarian organisations, including the International Organization for Migration (IOM), the United Nations Disaster Management Team, the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, the German Red Cross, ActionAid International, RedR India and RedR Australia. His professional journey has taken him to some of the world’s most challenging humanitarian environments. He contributed to humanitarian response efforts during the Rohingya refugee crisis in Bangladesh and worked on humanitarian challenges in Myanmar’s Rakhine State. He also supported recovery initiatives following the devastating 2015 earthquake in Nepal. His assignments with the Red Cross in Tajikistan, Kenya and Bangladesh remain among the significant milestones of his career. In Afghanistan, he contributed to climate action and disaster preparedness initiatives, while in Bangladesh, he worked on programmes aimed at helping vulnerable communities cope with recurring floods. He has also been involved in Anticipatory Action, an approach that uses forecasts and early warning systems to help communities prepare for disasters before they strike, reducing their potential impact. Born and raised in Bijhama in Uri, Jalil’s journey from a small border village to international humanitarian platforms has been shaped by his interest in social work and community welfare. As a youngster, he dreamt of representing his country in cricket. Although that ambition did not materialise, the discipline, determination and team spirit he developed through the game later became important foundations of his professional life. After completing his studies in sociology and social Work at the University of Kashmir, Jalil began his career as a schoolteacher. His growing interest in understanding human suffering and supporting vulnerable communities eventually drew him towards the humanitarian sector. Over nearly two decades, he has worked in around 15 countries and travelled to more than 30 nations, besides undertaking numerous international training programmes and professional courses in disaster management, climate change and humanitarian response.

stories.title: The US is in a bind: Arun Singh
stories.summary: The former India Ambassador to the US discusses the Republican setback in the recent US midterm elections, shifting public opinion, the Iran war’s impact on US power and the challenges facing India-US relations.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: In this episode of SpeakEasy with Amit Baruah, former Indian Ambassador to the United States Arun Singh discusses the political implications of the 2026 US midterm elections and their impact on American foreign policy.

With the Democrats making significant gains and voters turning against Donald Trump’s policies, Singh assesses what the results mean for the balance of power in Washington, the future of the Republican and Democratic parties, and Trump’s ability to pursue his political agenda.
The conversation examines the growing opposition to US support for Israel, the changing politics around Palestine, and the consequences of the war with Iran for American influence in West Asia.
Singh also discusses the strain on US relations with its Gulf allies, the possibility of a prolonged conflict with Iran, and the changing security calculations of countries in the region.

stories.headline: Three generations, three revolts: National Conference’s 80-year political battle against the Abdullah family
stories.title: Three generations, three revolts: National Conference’s 80-year political battle against the Abdullah family
stories.summary: The National Conference (NC), one of Jammu and Kashmir’s oldest political parties, is once again witnessing an internal revolt against the Abdullah family. Nearly two dozen party legislators have openly raised the banner of rebellion against Chief Minister Omar Abdullah and party president Dr Farooq Abdullah, while former Srinagar Lok Sabha MP Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi has taken the confrontation a step further by resigning from the party and his parliamentary seat. What makes the latest political crisis particularly significant is its historical context. This is not the first time that the Abdullah family has faced an open revolt within the National Conference. In fact, over the past eight decades, the party has witnessed three major rebellions against three generations of the Abdullah family—from its founder Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah, to his son Dr Farooq Abdullah, and now his grandson Omar Abdullah. The unfolding crisis raises a fundamental question: Is the National Conference heading towards another historic split, or will Dr Farooq Abdullah succeed in containing the rebellion before it threatens the stability of the government? The first major rebellion against the Abdullah family dates back to August 1953, when Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah, the founder of the National Conference and then Prime Minister of Jammu and Kashmir, was removed from office. At that time, Jammu and Kashmir had a Prime Minister rather than a Chief Minister, as the constitutional nomenclature had not yet been changed. Sheikh Abdullah’s government was dismissed on August 8, 1953, amid serious political differences with the Centre and allegations that he was pursuing an independent political course for Kashmir, including the possibility of independence and contacts with Pakistan. On August 9, 1953, Sheikh Abdullah was arrested and Bakshi Ghulam Mohammad, his close associate and then Deputy Prime Minister, was appointed in his place. Bakshi’s political break with Sheikh Abdullah marked the beginning of a major division within the National Conference. A section of the party's legislators supported the new leadership, while Sheikh Abdullah remained in detention for nearly 22 years, apart from periods of release. In 1975, following the historic Indira-Sheikh Accord, Sheikh Abdullah returned to power as Chief Minister. The then Congress Chief Minister, Mir Qasim, resigned to facilitate his return. The 1953 episode became the first major example of a political revolt that fundamentally altered the leadership of Jammu and Kashmir. The second major rebellion against the Abdullah family occurred on July 2, 1984, when 12 legislators withdrew their support from the government headed by Dr Farooq Abdullah. The political crisis had been building for months. Farooq Abdullah was facing growing opposition from within his own party, but he failed to address the grievances of the dissident legislators. The political atmosphere of that period was also marked by controversy surrounding Farooq Abdullah's personal style and public image. His association with film personalities, including actress Shabana Azmi, and his public motorcycle outings became subjects of political and media discussion. Shabana Azmi was later associated with the popular description of Farooq Abdullah as the "Disco Chief Minister". However, the fall of his government was the result of a political and legislative revolt rather than these social controversies. With 12 legislators withdrawing support, Farooq Abdullah lost his majority in the 78-member Assembly. Governor Jagmohan dismissed his government, paving the way for another dramatic political realignment. His brother-in-law, Ghulam Mohammad Shah, led the rebellion and formed a government with Congress support. Shah remained Chief Minister for approximately 20 months, until his government was dismissed in March 1986. He became popularly known as "Gul Shah", while his tenure was also associated with the controversial political expression "Gul Curfew" because he did not allow protests in Kashmir and put Srinagar city under strict curfew. He was known as the best administrator during his 20-month tenure. The 1984 revolt demonstrated that even a powerful political family could lose control of its own legislators when internal grievances were allowed to accumulate. This is not the first time that the Abdullah family has faced an open revolt within the National Conference.

The first major rebellion against the Abdullah family dates back to August 1953, when Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah, the founder of the National Conference and then Prime Minister of Jammu and Kashmir, was removed from office.
At that time, Jammu and Kashmir had a Prime Minister rather than a Chief Minister, as the constitutional nomenclature had not yet been changed.
